title: USMLE Step 2 CK
issuer: National Board of Medical Examiners / FSMB
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public USMLE Step 2 CK content outline. Not a capture of past test questions.

items.stem: A 62-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of 2 hours of crushing substernal chest pain that radiates to the left arm. He has hypertension and a 30-pack-year smoking history. On examination his blood pressure is 148/92 mm Hg and heart rate is 96/min. An ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads V2 through V4. He received aspirin 325 mg in the ambulance. Which of the following is the next best step in management?
options: Obtain an exercise stress test before discharge
Arrange for primary percutaneous coronary intervention within 90 minutes
Start oral metoprolol and observe on the ward
items.explanation: This patient has an acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction; the definitive therapy is rapid reperfusion with primary percutaneous coronary intervention, achievable within the 90-minute door-to-balloon window at an available center. Nitroglycerin is not the priority intervention and stress testing is inappropriate during an acute STEMI.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 34-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department 40 minutes after a motor vehicle collision. She has pain and swelling of the left knee. On examination the left knee is warm with a joint effusion. Range of motion is limited by pain. She is neurovascularly intact distally. A radiograph shows no fracture. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Open surgical exploration of the joint
Aspiration of the joint fluid for analysis
items.explanation: An acute hemarthrosis after trauma in a patient with no fracture requires joint aspiration to evaluate for intra-articular fracture or ligamentous injury and to relieve pressure. The remaining interventions are reserved for radiographic abnormalities or chronic synovial disease.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 58-year-old man is admitted with a 3-day history of productive cough, fever, and pleuritic right-sided chest pain. His temperature is 38.9 C, blood pressure is 105/68 mm Hg, pulse is 112/min, and respirations are 26/min. Crackles and dullness are present at the right lung base. A chest radiograph shows a homogeneous opacity with an air-fluid level in the right lower lobe. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 18,700/mm3 with left shift. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Observe with supportive care and repeat the radiograph in 6 weeks
Administer a single dose of oral azithromycin and discharge home
Perform pulmonary function testing before treatment
Initiate empiric antibiotic therapy with coverage of anaerobic organisms
items.explanation: The radiographic air-fluid level within a consolidated lobe indicates a lung abscess, which requires prompt initiation of antibiotics with anaerobic coverage along with airway drainage considerations. Discharge, delayed treatment, or pulmonary function testing would allow the infection to progress.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes mellitus is seen for a follow-up visit. She takes metformin and reports no symptoms. Her blood pressure is 132/78 mm Hg and body mass index is 31 kg/m2. Laboratory studies show an LDL cholesterol of 162 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 38 mg/dL, and triglycerides of 190 mg/dL after an 8-hour fast. She has no history of cardiovascular disease and does not smoke. Her 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk score is calculated at 7.5%. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Order coronary artery calcium scoring before any pharmacotherapy
Begin niacin therapy and repeat the lipid panel in 3 months
items.explanation: For primary prevention in an intermediate-risk patient with diabetes, current guidance supports measuring coronary artery calcium to refine risk stratification before committing to statin therapy; a score of zero supports deferring statins whereas a elevated score supports initiation. Ezetimibe and niacin are not first-line for primary prevention.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 70-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his family because of progressive confusion over 2 days. He has chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and was started on a prednisone burst 4 days ago. On examination his temperature is 37.0 C, blood pressure is 88/54 mm Hg, pulse is 124/min, and respirations are 24/min. Serum sodium is 126 mEq/L, potassium is 4.9 mEq/L, glucose is 92 mg/dL, and creatinine is 1.9 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion
items.explanation: An elderly patient taking chronic glucocorticoids who abruptly stops or tapers the drug can develop adrenal crisis, presenting with hypotension, hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and hypoglycemia from unopposed mineralocorticoid and stress-hormone deficiency. The remaining diagnoses do not explain the hypotension and electrolyte pattern in this context.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of fatigue, cold intolerance, weight gain of 9 kg, and constipation. She has no significant past medical history. On examination her temperature is 36.1 C, pulse is 54/min, and skin is dry with nonpitting edema of the face. Reflexes show a delayed relaxation phase. Her serum TSH is 38 mIU/L and free T4 is 0.3 ng/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
options: Observation with repeat thyroid function tests in 3 months
items.explanation: The clinical and laboratory findings are consistent with overt primary hypothyroidism, which is treated with oral levothyroxine replacement. Ablation, glucocorticoids, and watchful waiting would not correct the hormone deficiency and could worsen her symptoms.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 52-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of pain in both hands and wrists that is worse in the morning and improves as the day progresses. On examination there is symmetric swelling of the metacarpophalangeal joints and wrists bilaterally, with tenderness to palpation. Serum rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibodies are positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Refer for joint replacement surgery without medical therapy
Start prednisone alone without disease-modifying therapy
Start methotrexate with folic acid supplementation
items.explanation: Symmetric small-joint polyarthritis with positive serologies indicates rheumatoid arthritis, for which early initiation of a conventional synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drug such as methotrexate, paired with folic acid to reduce toxicity, is the cornerstone of treatment. Surgery and steroids alone are not appropriate primary management.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 42-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of severe pain and swelling of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint that began abruptly 12 hours ago after a dinner at which he consumed shellfish and alcohol. He has not had a similar episode before. On examination the joint is erythematous, warm, and exquisitely tender; passive movement is limited by pain. Serum uric acid is 10.8 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate acute treatment?
items.explanation: An acute gout flare is treated symptomatically with colchicine, an NSAID, or a corticosteroid; urate-lowering agents such as allopurinol, probenecid, and lesinurad are maintenance therapies that should not be started during an acute attack because they can prolong the flare.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 66-year-old man with a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes is admitted for an acute decompensation with dyspnea at rest. On examination he has bilateral crackles, jugular venous distention, and a 3+ pitting edema of the lower extremities. He is started on intravenous furosemide. Which of the following additional therapies has been shown to reduce cardiovascular mortality and hospitalizations in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes?
items.explanation: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors such as empagliflozin reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalizations across the spectrum of ejection fraction, including patients with concomitant type 2 diabetes. The other diabetes agents lack this established mortality benefit in heart failure.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 48-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of epigastric burning that improves when she eats and wakes her at night. She takes ibuprofen for osteoarthritis. On examination there is mild epigastric tenderness. Testing for Helicobacter pylori antigen in the stool is positive. An upper gastrointestinal endoscopy shows a 1.2-cm clean-based duodenal ulcer without bleeding. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Pantoprazole plus amoxicillin, clarithromycin, and bismuth subsalicylate for 14 days
items.explanation: A Helicobacter pylori-positive duodenal ulcer requires eradication therapy with a proton pump inhibitor plus bismuth and dual antibiotics for 14 days, followed by confirmation of eradication. Acid suppression alone leaves the organism untreated, and ranitidine has been withdrawn from the market.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 63-year-old woman is admitted with a serum calcium concentration of 13.4 mg/dL. She has a history of metastatic breast cancer. On examination she is dehydrated, and she reports nausea, constipation, and confusion. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
items.explanation: Hypercalcemia of malignancy requires immediate isotonic intravenous saline rehydration to restore volume and promote calciuresis before other agents such as calcitonin or bisphosphonates are used. Diuresing a dehydrated patient without prior hydration would worsen hypercalcemia.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 55-year-old man is admitted with a serum potassium concentration of 7.1 mEq/L. He has chronic kidney disease. An ECG shows peaked T waves and a widened QRS complex. He reports no chest pain. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate treatment?
items.explanation: Severe hyperkalemia with ECG changes is a medical emergency treated first with intravenous calcium gluconate to stabilize the cardiac membrane, followed by therapies that shift potassium intracellularly and ultimately remove it from the body. Insulin and resin therapy act too slowly to protect the myocardium in the immediate period.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine examination. She feels well. She has never been screened for colorectal cancer. She has no family history of colorectal cancer and no personal history of inflammatory bowel disease. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening recommendation?
options: Fecal immunochemical testing annually beginning at age 45
Flexible sigmoidoscopy every 5 years beginning at age 60
items.explanation: Average-risk adults should begin colorectal cancer screening at age 45; annual fecal immunochemical testing is an accepted option, as is colonoscopy every 10 years. Carcinoembryonic antigen is not a screening test, and waiting until age 60 is no longer recommended.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman is seen 6 days after an upper respiratory tract infection for a 2-day history of dark urine, facial puffiness in the morning, and decreased urine output. Blood pressure is 152/94 mm Hg. Laboratory studies show creatinine of 2.4 mg/dL, which had been 0.8 mg/dL 2 weeks earlier, and urinalysis shows dysmorphic red blood cells and red blood cell casts. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic study?
options: 24-hour urine protein measurement without further evaluation
items.explanation: The presentation of nephritic syndrome with dysmorphic red cells and red blood cell casts after an infection indicates glomerulonephritis requiring renal biopsy to establish the histologic diagnosis and guide therapy. Ultrasonography is reserved for suspected obstruction, and urine culture does not explain an active sediment.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 72-year-old woman is admitted with confusion and a fever of 39.1 C. On examination she has a new murmur, splinter hemorrhages, and Janeway lesions on the palms. Blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in clusters from two separate sets. Which of the following is the most appropriate antibiotic regimen?
items.explanation: Staphylococcal infective endocarditis with systemic embolic stigmata requires intravenous vancomycin with an aminoglycoside for synergistic coverage pending identification and susceptibility testing; nafcillin alone is insufficient empirically in this setting, and monotherapy with amoxicillin or ciprofloxacin does not cover resistant staphylococci.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Internal Medicine

items.stem: A 34-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle collision. His Glasgow Coma Scale score is 6 and his blood pressure is 98/62 mm Hg. He has obvious facial trauma with stridor and gurgling. There is no audible breath sound over the right hemithorax. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate action?
options: Insert an oral airway and administer humidified oxygen
Obtain a chest radiograph before intervention
Perform a needle thoracostomy on the left side
Establish a definitive airway with endotracheal intubation
items.explanation: An unconscious trauma patient with stridor, gurgling, and hypoxia requires immediate securing of the airway, since blood and secretions are compromising ventilation; secondary survey and imaging come after the airway is controlled. The clinical picture indicates airway compromise rather than isolated pneumothorax.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 45-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 30 minutes after a fall from a scaffold. He reports severe abdominal pain. His blood pressure is 92/64 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. The abdomen is tender and distended. Focused assessment with sonography for trauma examination shows free fluid in the peritoneal cavity. A chest radiograph shows a normal diaphragm. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast after fluid resuscitation
Repeat focused assessment with sonography for trauma in 2 hours
items.explanation: A hemodynamically stable patient with a positive FAST and blunt abdominal trauma requires contrast-enhanced CT for organ-specific diagnosis before operative planning; unstable patients proceed directly to laparotomy, and repeat sonography delays needed care.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 66-year-old woman is admitted with a 1-day history of crampy abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, and obstipation. She had open appendectomy 30 years ago. On examination her abdomen is distended and tympanitic, with high-pitched tinkling bowel sounds. An abdominal radiograph shows multiple air-fluid levels and a paucity of gas in the distal colon. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Nothing by mouth, nasogastric decompression, and intravenous fluid resuscitation
items.explanation: A patient with a adhesive small bowel obstruction and no signs of strangulation is managed nonoperatively with bowel rest, nasogastric tube decompression, and intravenous fluids while being observed for deterioration; surgery is reserved for peritonitis, ischemia, or failure to resolve.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 25-year-old man is admitted with severe pain and swelling of the left calf after a skiing injury. On examination the calf is tense and tender, and pain is elicited with passive dorsiflexion of the toes. Pulses are palpable distally. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Elevation of the leg and application of ice
Measurement of compartment pressures followed by fasciotomy if elevated
Duplex ultrasonography of the deep veins
Observation with serial examinations every 4 hours
items.explanation: Suspected acute compartment syndrome requires immediate measurement of intracompartmental pressures with urgent fasciotomy if pressures are elevated; the presence of distal pulses does not exclude the diagnosis, and delay or conservative measures risk muscle necrosis and amputation.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 58-year-old man is admitted with sudden severe tearing pain in the chest radiating to the back. He has a history of poorly controlled hypertension. On examination his blood pressure is 182/104 mm Hg in the right arm and 140/78 mm Hg in the left arm. Which of the following is the most appropriate diagnostic study?
items.explanation: Tearing chest pain with a blood pressure differential between arms in a hypertensive patient indicates acute aortic dissection, which is diagnosed urgently with CT angiography of the chest and requires blood pressure and heart rate control; stress testing is contraindicated in the acute setting.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 62-year-old man is admitted with acute pain in the left lower quadrant of the abdomen, fever, and constipation of 3 days' duration. His temperature is 38.6 C and there is tenderness with guarding in the left lower quadrant. A CT scan shows a 4-cm colonic wall thickening with pericolic fat stranding and a small extraluminal air collection. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Colonoscopy with biopsy of the affected segment
Nothing by mouth, intravenous antibiotics, and percutaneous drainage if a discrete collection is present
Outpatient oral antibiotics with follow-up in 2 weeks
items.explanation: Uncomplicated acute diverticulitis with a small contained extraluminal air collection is managed conservatively with bowel rest and intravenous antibiotics plus percutaneous drainage when a drainable collection exists; resection is reserved for free perforation or failure of medical therapy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 48-year-old man is admitted with right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice of 2 days' duration. His temperature is 39.1 C, and there is tenderness in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies show a leukocyte count of 16,400/mm3, total bilirubin of 4.8 mg/dL, and alkaline phosphatase of 340 U/L. Ultrasonography shows a dilated common bile duct of 12 mm with stones within it. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography as the first intervention
Emergent endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with sphincterotomy and stone extraction
Open common bile duct exploration in the operating room without imaging
items.explanation: Ascending cholangitis with obstructing choledocholithiasis requires urgent biliary decompression, most commonly with emergent ERCP and stone extraction after initial resuscitation and antibiotics; delay risks progression to septic shock.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 70-year-old man is admitted with a 3-day history of fever, chills, and tenderness of the right calf. He had a total knee arthroplasty 6 weeks ago. On examination the right calf is swollen, warm, and tender, and homans sign is present. Duplex ultrasonography confirms a deep vein thrombosis of the popliteal vein. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Intravenous unfractionated heparin followed by a vitamin K antagonist
Inferior vena cava filter placement without anticoagulation
items.explanation: Acute proximal deep vein thrombosis requires therapeutic anticoagulation, initiated with unfractionated heparin in the inpatient setting and transitioned to a vitamin K antagonist or direct oral anticoagulant; aspirin alone is insufficient and filters are reserved for anticoagulation contraindications.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department after a fall while rock climbing. She reports pain and an inability to bear weight on the right arm. On examination there is tenderness and swelling over the anatomical snuffbox. A radiograph of the wrist shows no fracture. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Splinting with aspirin and return to activity as tolerated
Open reduction and internal fixation without repeat imaging
Immobilization in a thumb spica cast and repeat imaging in 2 weeks
items.explanation: Tenderness over the anatomical snuffbox after trauma indicates a scaphoid fracture that may be radiographically occult; the standard approach is thumb spica immobilization with follow-up imaging or advanced imaging to confirm the fracture. Premature return to activity risks nonunion and avascular necrosis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman is admitted with a 2-day history of progressive jaundice, pale stools, and dark urine. On examination there is a palpable, nontender mass in the right upper quadrant. Laboratory studies show a total bilirubin of 9.2 mg/dL and an alkaline phosphatase of 420 U/L. A CT scan shows a mass in the head of the pancreas with dilatation of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Endoscopic biliary stent placement with brushings for cytology
items.explanation: Painless obstructive jaundice from a pancreatic head mass requires endoscopic decompression with stent placement and cytologic brushing to obtain tissue diagnosis before any oncologic surgery; external drainage or immediate major resection without tissue confirmation is not appropriate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 40-year-old man is admitted with a 2-day history of right lower quadrant pain, anorexia, and low-grade fever. On examination there is tenderness at McBurney point with rebound and guarding. A CT scan shows an inflamed appendix with a small amount of periappendiceal fat stranding but no abscess. He has no contraindications to surgery. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Intravenous antibiotics alone with interval appendectomy in 6 weeks
items.explanation: Uncomplicated acute appendicitis without abscess in a surgical candidate is treated with urgent appendectomy, preferably laparoscopically; antibiotics alone are reserved for selected uncomplicated cases or as a bridge when an abscess requires drainage first.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 55-year-old man is admitted with a 3-day history of fever, chills, and a painful, erythematous swelling of the perineum that has progressed rapidly. On examination the skin of the perineum is necrotic with crepitus, and the patient is toxic with a temperature of 39.4 C and blood pressure of 94/58 mm Hg. He has type 2 diabetes mellitus. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Broad-spectrum antibiotics alone with wound care
Immediate surgical debridement with broad-spectrum antibiotics and resuscitation
Incision and drainage of a superficial abscess under local anesthesia
items.explanation: Necrotizing soft tissue infection of the perineum, also known as Fournier gangrene, is a surgical emergency requiring immediate wide debridement together with aggressive resuscitation and broad-spectrum antibiotics; antibiotics or hyperbaric oxygen alone cannot control the spreading necrosis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 30-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a stab wound to the left anterior chest. On examination his blood pressure is 90/60 mm Hg, pulse is 128/min, and there is a 2-cm wound at the left fourth intercostal space, parasternal. Jugular venous distention is present. Which of the following is the most appropriate immediate intervention?
items.explanation: Penetrating chest trauma with hypotension, tachycardia, and jugular venous distention indicates cardiac tamponade, which requires immediate pericardiocentesis or thoracotomy to relieve the tamponade; imaging would delay life-saving decompression.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman is admitted with a 6-month history of a painless lump in the right breast. On examination there is a 3-cm firm mass in the upper outer quadrant of the right breast with nipple retraction. Axillary lymph nodes are not palpable. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Mammography followed by core needle biopsy
items.explanation: A suspicious solid breast mass with skin or nipple changes requires diagnostic mammography followed by core needle biopsy for tissue diagnosis before any surgical planning; fine-needle aspiration is insufficient for full histologic grading and receptor status.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 50-year-old man is admitted with a 1-day history of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, and vomiting. He has a history of alcohol use disorder and gallstones. On examination there is epigastric tenderness with guarding. Serum lipase is 1,800 U/L and calcium is 7.4 mg/dL. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Aggressive intravenous fluid resuscitation with pain control and bowel rest
Oral feeding with pancreatic enzyme supplementation
items.explanation: Acute pancreatitis is initially managed supportively with aggressive intravenous crystalloid resuscitation, analgesia, and bowel rest; urgent ERCP is reserved for concurrent cholangitis or persistent common bile duct obstruction, and cholecystectomy is deferred until the acute episode resolves in gallstone pancreatitis without cholangitis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Surgery and Emergency Medicine

items.stem: A 2-day-old newborn develops respiratory distress with tachypnea, nasal flaring, and grunting shortly after birth. He was born at term via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery to a mother with gestational diabetes. On examination he has retractions but no cyanosis, and breath sounds are clear bilaterally. A chest radiograph shows hyperinflation with mild perihilar streaking and no pleural effusion. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
items.explanation: A term or late-preterm newborn, especially after cesarean delivery or maternal diabetes, who develops early respiratory distress with hyperinflation and perihilar streaking most likely has transient tachypnea of the newborn from delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid; the condition is self-limited with supportive care.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 5-day history of fever up to 40 C, a rash on both legs that started as erythematous macules and progressed to vesicles, and irritability. His mother reports no immunizations. On examination there are grouped vesicles on an erythematous base, with some lesions showing central umbilication. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Supportive care with antipyretics and observation
items.explanation: An unimmunized child with a vesiculopustular rash in crops, especially with fever and systemic symptoms, suggests disseminated varicella, which requires oral or intravenous acyclovir depending on severity; supportive care alone risks visceral complications, and antibiotics or topical steroids are inappropriate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 6-year-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of a 3-day history of fever to 39.8 C, bilateral conjunctival injection without exudate, a strawberry tongue, and erythema of the hands and feet. Cervical lymphadenopathy is present. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Obtain a throat culture and start azithromycin
Order an echocardiogram only and observe
items.explanation: The clinical criteria indicate Kawasaki disease, which requires treatment within 10 days of fever with intravenous immunoglobulin and aspirin to reduce the risk of coronary artery aneurysms; delaying therapy for additional testing or using steroids or antibiotics alone is not appropriate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 16-year-old girl is brought to the physician because of a 4-month history of fatigue. Her temperature is 36.8 C, pulse is 58/min, and blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg. She has thin skin with fine hair over her back and a BMI of 16 kg/m2. Her parents report she has been restricting food intake and exercising excessively. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Inpatient medical stabilization with a structured refeeding program
Outpatient cognitive behavioral therapy without medical evaluation
Initiation of high-calorie oral supplements without monitoring
items.explanation: An adolescent with anorexia nervosa and a significantly low BMI with bradycardia requires inpatient medical stabilization including monitored refeeding to prevent refeeding syndrome, electrolyte shifts, and cardiac complications before outpatient psychological therapy can begin.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, is admitted at 39 weeks of gestation for labor. She screened positive for group B Streptococcus during this pregnancy. She develops a fever of 38.4 C with uterine tenderness during labor, and the fetal heart rate is 170/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: Intrapartum fever with uterine tenderness and fetal tachycardia in a group B Streptococcus-positive patient indicates chorioamnionitis, which is treated with intravenous ampicillin plus gentamicin; oral therapy is inadequate for this serious intrauterine infection.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 32-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, at 34 weeks of gestation is admitted with a blood pressure of 168/108 mm Hg, headache, and visual changes. Laboratory studies show a platelet count of 95,000/mm3, AST of 88 U/L, and urine protein of 3+ by dipstick. Her fetus is alive and in cephalic presentation. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Immediate cesarean delivery regardless of cervical status
Magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis and delivery of the fetus
Bed rest at home with weekly blood pressure checks
items.explanation: Severe features of preeclampsia, including blood pressure of 160/110 mm Hg, neurologic symptoms, thrombocytopenia, and hepatic involvement, require magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis and definitive treatment is delivery, which at 34 weeks follows stabilization; outpatient management is unsafe.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 26-year-old woman, gravida 2 para 1, at 12 weeks of gestation presents with vaginal bleeding and left lower quadrant pain. Her blood pressure is 100/60 mm Hg and pulse is 110/min. A urine pregnancy test is positive. Transvaginal ultrasonography shows an empty uterus with a complex adnexal mass and free fluid in the cul-de-sac. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Expectant management with serial human chorionic gonadotropin levels
items.explanation: A hemodynamically unstable woman with an adnexal mass and free peritoneal fluid consistent with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy requires emergency surgery to control hemorrhage; methotrexate is reserved for hemodynamically stable patients with confirmed unruptured ectopic pregnancy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 4-day-old newborn is noted to have lethargy, poor feeding, and jaundice that extends to the palms and soles. His mother is O-negative and did not receive Rho(D) immune globulin during this pregnancy. The infant's total bilirubin is 18 mg/dL and direct antiglobulin test is positive. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: A newborn with early-onset hyperbilirubinemia from Rh hemolytic disease, with a bilirubin level in the exchange range and evidence of kernicterus risk, requires exchange transfusion to rapidly lower bilirubin and prevent irreversible neurologic injury; phototherapy alone is insufficient at this level.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 5-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of a 2-day history of fever and sore throat. On examination the pharynx is erythematous with exudate and the cervical lymph nodes are enlarged. A rapid antigen detection test for group A Streptococcus is positive. He has no known drug allergies. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: Streptococcal pharyngitis in a child requires a 10-day course of penicillin V to eradicate the organism and prevent acute rheumatic fever; macrolides are reserved for penicillin-allergic patients, and shorter courses risk incomplete eradication.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 20-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of irregular menses and acne. On examination she has hirsutism and a BMI of 34 kg/m2. Her serum testosterone is mildly elevated, and a pelvic ultrasonogram shows bilaterally enlarged ovaries with multiple peripheral follicles. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial management?
options: Combined oral contraceptive pills and lifestyle modification
items.explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome in an anovulatory woman seeking cycle regulation is initially managed with combined oral contraceptives to restore regular menses and reduce androgen effects, plus lifestyle modification for weight; surgical or glucocorticoid approaches are not first-line.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 40-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 3-month history of a bloody nipple discharge from the left breast. On examination there is a small amount of serosanguineous discharge from the left nipple, and no mass is palpable. A mammogram shows a 5-mm group of calcifications in the left breast. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Diagnostic ductography followed by excisional biopsy of the ductal system
Observation with repeat mammography in 12 months
Fine-needle aspiration of the nipple discharge
items.explanation: Spontaneous unilateral bloody nipple discharge with mammographic calcifications in a woman of this age raises concern for intraductal papilloma or ductal carcinoma in situ, requiring ductography and excisional biopsy of the involved ducts for definitive diagnosis; antibiotic therapy and watchful waiting are inappropriate.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 6-month history of heavy menstrual bleeding with clots, lasting 8 days each cycle. She has no other medical history. Her hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume is 76 fL. Pelvic examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial diagnostic evaluation?
options: Thyroid-stimulating hormone, complete blood count, and coagulation studies
items.explanation: Abnormal uterine bleeding in a young woman requires initial evaluation for systemic causes including thyroid dysfunction, anemia, and coagulopathies such as von Willebrand disease, using laboratory studies before proceeding to invasive uterine evaluation.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 2-day-old newborn is noted to have ambiguous genitalia. On examination the clitoromegaly is present with a single perineal opening and palpable gonads in the inguinal regions. Serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone is markedly elevated, and karyotype reveals 46,XX. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
options: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency
items.explanation: A 46,XX newborn with ambiguous genitalia and markedly elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone has classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia from 21-hydroxylase deficiency, in which excess adrenal androgens virilize the external genitalia of a genetic female; the other conditions do not produce this biochemical profile.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, at 28 weeks of gestation is admitted with a 2-day history of vaginal drainage of clear fluid. A nitrazine test of the fluid is positive, and ferning is observed on microscopic examination. Her temperature is 37.2 C and fetal heart rate is 148/min. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Expectant management with corticosteroids and observation for labor
Administration of oxytocin to induce labor
items.explanation: Premature rupture of membranes at 28 weeks without labor, infection, or fetal distress is managed expectantly with corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity, monitoring for chorioamnionitis, and attempts to prolong gestation; early delivery before viability risks neonatal morbidity.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 14-year-old girl is brought to the physician by her mother because she has not yet begun menstruating. Her height is 145 cm and weight is 42 kg. On examination there is no axillary or pubic hair, and breast development is Tanner stage 2. Her mother reports that she herself began menstruating at age 15. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step?
options: Reassurance with observation over the next 6 to 12 months
items.explanation: A girl with a normal growth pattern, early breast development, and a family history of delayed menarche who is 14 years old without menarche is likely constitutionally delayed; since secondary sexual characteristics are progressing, reassurance with periodic follow-up is appropriate before pursuing hormonal evaluation or treatment.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Pediatrics and Obstetrics-Gynecology

items.stem: A 55-year-old woman is admitted with a fever of 39.2 C, diaphoresis, and muscle rigidity. She was started on a monoamine oxidase inhibitor 2 weeks ago for depression and took meperidine for abdominal pain in the emergency department 4 hours ago. On examination she is agitated with hyperreflexia and clonus. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: The combination of a monoamine oxidase inhibitor with meperidine precipitates serotonin syndrome, presenting with hyperthermia, rigidity, clonus, and autonomic instability; treatment requires discontinuation of serotonergic agents with cyproheptadine as a serotonin antagonist and supportive cooling, with dantrolene for severe rigidity.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by his family because of bizarre behavior over 3 days. He was started on haloperidol for new-onset psychosis 1 week ago. On examination he has sustained involuntary contraction of the neck muscles with deviation of the eyes and trismus. He is afebrile with stable vital signs. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Cessation of haloperidol with observation only
items.explanation: Acute dystonic reaction from a first-generation antipsychotic presents with painful muscle spasms and oculogyric deviation and is treated promptly with an anticholinergic agent such as diphenhydramine or benztropine; benzodiazepines alone are not the specific antidote.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman comes to the physician because of recurrent episodes of palpitations, sweating, and a fear of dying that last about 10 minutes and occur several times a week. She avoids crowded places because of these episodes. Physical examination and an ECG are unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Cognitive behavioral therapy combined with a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
items.explanation: Panic disorder is best treated with cognitive behavioral therapy plus a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor; long-term benzodiazepine therapy risks dependence, and watchful waiting leaves the patient functionally impaired.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 40-year-old man is admitted with tremor, diaphoresis, and tachycardia that began 48 hours after his last drink. He has a history of daily alcohol use for 10 years. On examination his blood pressure is 158/92 mm Hg and pulse is 118/min. He is oriented but agitated. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: Alcohol withdrawal with autonomic hyperactivity is treated with a benzodiazepine such as chlordiazepoxide to prevent seizures and delirium tremens, along with thiamine to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy; antipsychotics lower the seizure threshold and disulfiram is used only for maintenance sobriety, not acute withdrawal.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 22-year-old man is brought to the emergency department by police after he attempted to jump from a bridge. He has a history of bipolar disorder and says he no longer wants to live. He has a detailed plan, has secured the means, and denies any reason to live. His mental status examination is otherwise coherent. Which of the following is the most appropriate disposition?
options: Outpatient follow-up with a psychiatrist within 1 week
Release to police custody without evaluation
Prescription for an SSRI with outpatient therapy
items.explanation: An individual with acute suicidal ideation, a specific plan, acquired means, and no protective factors after a recent attempt poses an imminent risk and requires involuntary psychiatric hospitalization for safety; outpatient management or release is unsafe.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 30-year-old woman is seen for a routine examination. She has a 12-pack-year smoking history and currently smokes 1 pack per day. She wants to quit and asks about pharmacotherapy. She has no contraindications. Which of the following is the most appropriate recommendation?
options: Nicotine replacement therapy alone without a quit date
items.explanation: Smoking cessation is best supported by combining pharmacotherapy such as varenicline or bupropion with behavioral counseling, which substantially increases quit rates compared with either alone; spirometry is not a cessation strategy.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the physician by his mother because of difficulty concentrating at school for the past year. He is restless, frequently leaves his seat, and interrupts others. Symptoms are present in multiple settings and impair his academic performance. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Stimulant medication combined with behavioral therapy and parent training
Placement in special education without other intervention
items.explanation: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder in an adolescent with cross-setting symptoms and functional impairment is treated with a combination of medication, typically a stimulant, and behavioral interventions including parent training; antipsychotics are not indicated and deferral allows worsening academic and social outcomes.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 45-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 4-month history of depressed mood, anhedonia, insomnia, poor appetite, and difficulty concentrating. She has no prior psychiatric history and denies suicidal ideation. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?
options: Cognitive behavioral therapy or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor
items.explanation: A first episode of moderate major depressive disorder without psychotic features or suicidality is treated with evidence-based psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy or with an SSRI; lithium and electroconvulsive therapy are reserved for treatment-resistant or severe cases.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 50-year-old man comes to the physician for a routine examination. He has a 25-pack-year smoking history and quit smoking 2 years ago. He has no symptoms. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening recommendation?
options: Low-dose CT scan of the chest annually
items.explanation: An adult aged 50 to 80 with a 20 pack-year history who has quit within the past 15 years meets criteria for annual low-dose CT lung cancer screening; chest radiographs and sputum cytology have not been shown to reduce mortality.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 35-year-old woman comes to the physician for a routine examination. She has no symptoms and no significant medical history. She has never been screened for HIV. Physical examination is unremarkable. Which of the following is the most appropriate screening recommendation?
options: Screen all adults aged 15 to 65 at least once
Screen only if she reports high-risk behavior
items.explanation: All adolescents and adults aged 15 to 65 should be screened for HIV at least once regardless of perceived risk, with selective rescreening for those at ongoing higher risk; annual screening for everyone is not recommended in the general population.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 42-year-old man comes to the physician because of a 3-day history of pain and swelling of the left knee. On examination the joint is erythematous and warm with an effusion. Aspiration of the joint fluid shows negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals and a leukocyte count of 55,000/mm3. Gram stain shows no organisms. He has a history of recurrent kidney stones. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
items.explanation: The aspiration findings confirm acute gouty arthritis, which is treated with anti-inflammatory agents such as colchicine or NSAIDs; antibiotics are reserved for septic arthritis when infection is confirmed or strongly suspected, and urate-lowering therapy is maintenance treatment.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 60-year-old man comes to the physician for a routine examination. He has hypertension and a total cholesterol of 240 mg/dL. He has no history of cardiovascular disease and does not smoke. His 10-year atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk score is 12%. Which of the following is the most appropriate management?
options: Moderate-intensity statin therapy with lifestyle modification
No pharmacotherapy with repeat lipid panel in 5 years
items.explanation: An intermediate-to-high-risk primary prevention patient with an LDL above threshold and a 10-year risk of 7.5% or greater should begin moderate-intensity statin therapy with lifestyle counseling; aspirin is not indicated solely for lipid risk reduction and deferred follow-up allows progression of atherosclerosis.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 28-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 2-year history of binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting, exercise abuse, and fear of weight gain. Her body mass index is 19 kg/m2 and her serum potassium is 3.1 mEq/L. Dental enamel erosion is noted on examination. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
options: Nutritional rehabilitation with cognitive behavioral therapy and electrolyte monitoring
Inpatient medical admission for forced feeding only
items.explanation: Bulimia nervosa is treated with nutritional rehabilitation and evidence-based psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy, with correction and monitoring of electrolyte disturbances and dental complications; there is no indication for forced feeding or mood stabilizers in this context.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 30-year-old primigravida at 28 weeks of gestation is seen for a routine prenatal visit. She reports that her partner has been physically abusive. She has facial bruising and is reluctant to involve authorities. Which of the following is the most appropriate response?
options: Assess her safety, document findings, and provide resources for domestic violence support
Notify her partner with her consent to discuss the situation
Advise her to leave immediately without further evaluation
Refer her to a family law attorney only
items.explanation: Intimate partner violence in pregnancy requires a confidential safety assessment, careful documentation, and provision of resources and referrals; involving the abuser or issuing directives without support can increase danger to the patient.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine

items.stem: A 24-year-old graduate student is brought to the emergency department by friends because of 3 days of insomnia, grandiose beliefs that he can communicate telepathically, and pressured speech. He has a family history of bipolar disorder. On examination he is distractible with flight of ideas. He denies suicidal ideation but has not eaten or slept for days. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacologic treatment?
options: Lithium carbonate or another mood stabilizer
items.explanation: A manic episode with grandiosity, pressured speech, and reduced need for sleep in a patient with a family history of bipolar disorder is treated with a mood stabilizer such as lithium or valproate, with benzodiazepines for agitation as adjuncts; antidepressant monotherapy can worsen mania.
items.reference: USMLE Step 2 CK Content Outline - Psychiatry and Preventive Medicine
